artworks.title: The Wounded Philoctetes
artworks.description: Abildgaard's Copenhagen canvas — the Lemnos exile whose bow the Little Iliad must fetch before Troy can fall.

artworks.title: The Isolation of Philoctetes on Lemnos
artworks.description: Rémond's Toulouse landscape — the abandoned archer alone with Heracles' weapons until Odysseus and Diomedes return.

artworks.title: The Building of the Trojan Horse
artworks.description: Tiepolo's Epeius at work — the wooden horse that closes the Little Iliad and opens the sack.

artworks.title: Neoptolemus Killing Priam (Attic black-figure amphora)
artworks.artist: Attributed to the Class of Cambridge 49
artworks.description: Attic amphora — Achilles' son fetched from Scyros in the Little Iliad, already the killer of Priam at the altar.

artworks.title: Philoctetes on the Island of Lemnos
artworks.description: Lethière's Neoclassical Lemnos — the indispensable archer the cycle must reclaim before Paris falls to Heracles' arrows.

popCulture.title: Little Iliad
popCulture.description: The lost Epic Cycle poem after Achilles' death — Philoctetes fetched, Paris slain, Helenus captured, Neoptolemus armed, and the wooden horse built.

popCulture.title: Philoctetes (Sophocles play)
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' prize-winning tragedy of the Lemnos retrieval — Odysseus' craft and Neoptolemus' conscience over the bow Troy cannot fall without.

popCulture.title: Epic Cycle
popCulture.description: The Trojan cycle that slots the Little Iliad between Aethiopis and Iliou persis — the stratagems that finish what Homer left standing.
